title: Infrastructure configuration defaults in Settings diverge from docker-compose
description: Settings class defines default connection URLs (RABBITMQ_URL with guest:guest, DATABASE_URL with hardcoded credentials) while docker-compose.yml configures services with different credentials (janus:janus for both). database.py independently reads from os.getenv with yet another fallback. This creates 3 potential sources of truth for the same credentials, leading to connection failures when services start with Settings defaults against docker-compose infrastructure.
root_cause: Phase 3.2 Sub-Agent A generates Settings with generic defaults (guest:guest for RabbitMQ is the vendor default), while Sub-Agent B generates docker-compose with project-specific credentials. The two sub-agents have no mechanism to share the credential values. Phase 3.4 (Reconcile) does not verify that Settings defaults match docker-compose environment variables.
recommendation: In Phase 3.4 (Reconcile), add a cross-reference check: for each infrastructure service in docker-compose.yml, verify that the corresponding Settings field's default value matches the docker-compose credentials. Generate a .env.example file that documents all environment variables with their expected values. Ensure database.py reads from Settings instead of os.getenv.
